# Settings — Developers

Available on **All plans**.

## Deep links — where to find them

The Deep links block lives at **Joy Admin → Settings → Developers → Deep links** — this is the primary, canonical location. (A read-only summary also surfaces on the General settings page, but the block itself and any editing happen under **Developers**.) When a merchant asks "where are the deep links / where do I get the link", route them to **Settings → Developers**.

## Anchors (no setup needed)

- `#joy-home` — main widget home
- `#joy-ways-to-earn`
- `#joy-ways-to-redeem`
- `#joy-referral-program`

## Setup

**Shopify Admin → Online Store → Navigation → [Main menu / Footer] → Add menu item** → name (e.g., Rewards) + URL (paste `#joy-home`). Save → clicking that menu item opens the widget.

You can disable the floating widget button entirely once deeplinks are set up.

---

Available on **Advanced+**. Add/remove customer points by adding a Shopify tag.

## Enable

**Settings → Developers → Manage Tags** toggle on.

## Tag syntax

```
Joy: Add 500 - Place order #111 via POS
Joy: Subtract 100 - Refund
```

The number after Add/Subtract adjusts the balance; the comment tracks the reason.

Useful in **Shopify Flow** workflows that auto-tag customers with these strings — Joy reads tags and updates balances. Provides flexibility beyond the Joy API.

---

Use the official `joyso-hydrogen-sdk` npm package.

## Steps

1. **Joy Admin → Settings → Developers → Enable Custom Storefront development**
2. Install `joyso-hydrogen-sdk` in your Hydrogen project
3. In `app/root.jsx`: add the loader to fetch Joy data
4. Initialize Joy in root layout
5. Add CSP whitelist in `entry.server.jsx`
6. Optional CSS fix: Hydrogen quickstart uses `box-sizing: content-box` which can warp the floating button — add corrective CSS

Non-Plus stores can test with Storefront API key from a custom app in dev environment.

---

**Settings → Developers → Manage keys → Generate key** — creates App ID + Secret key.

**Important:** Generating a new key invalidates any previous key. If another app already uses the old credentials, you must update them.

---

## AI assistant access — manage loyalty via Claude & ChatGPT (Joy MCP)

Joy connects to AI assistants that support **MCP (Model Context Protocol) with remote + OAuth** — confirmed working with **Claude** and **ChatGPT**. Any other MCP-compatible AI assistant with the same remote+OAuth support should in theory also connect, but this isn't verified case-by-case — don't promise support for a specific third-party AI tool without checking first.

**Enable at:** Joy Admin → Settings → Developers → connect AI assistant. Full setup guide: `help.joy.so/settings/developers/connect-claude-and-chatgpt/`.

**What it's for:** a merchant who already works inside an AI assistant (with their own business context loaded) can ask it to pull loyalty data or make changes, instead of switching over to the Joy admin. Common use cases: a weekly/monthly loyalty summary, looking up or updating a specific customer's points/tier, or issuing a reward.

**Permission levels:**
- **Read-only** — the AI assistant can only view data (points, tiers, program info); it cannot make changes.
- **Full access** — the AI assistant can add/subtract points, change tiers, issue rewards, and adjust point balances. Any balance change shows a before/after preview before it's applied.

This is a new integration — scope may expand over time, so treat it as an evolving capability rather than a fixed, final feature list.

## Related
- kb_settings-general (deep links shown in General settings)
- kb_integrations-mobile (Shopney, Tapcart use API keys)
- kb_integrations-shopify-flow (Magic Tags via Flow)
- kb_widget (widget vs deeplink anchors)

---

**Plan required: Joy Ultimate ($499/mo) — effective September 17, 2025.**

REST API v2 and Webhook API are **exclusively available on the Ultimate plan**. Lower plans (Starter, Essential, Advanced) will receive a `PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` error.

## What's included with Ultimate API access

- **REST API v2** — manage customers, point transactions, rewards, VIP tiers, referrals
- **Webhook API** — real-time notifications for 20+ loyalty events (points earned, tier upgraded, coupon used, etc.)
- **Headless / Hydrogen** support
- Cursor-based pagination, comprehensive error handling, automatic data filtering

## Authentication

Credentials are found in **Settings → Developers → Manage keys → Generate key** (App ID + Secret Key).

Official docs: `devdocs.joy.so/joy-rest-api-v2/rest-api-v2`

## Upgrade path

**Settings → Subscription → All Plans** to upgrade to Ultimate.

# Chat Apps, Theme Integration, and Inventory Apps

Surface loyalty profile inside support conversations.

## Synced fields

| Field | Chatty | Gorgias |
|---|---|---|
| Member type / status | ✅ | ✅ |
| VIP tier | ✅ | ✅ |
| Points balance | ✅ | ✅ |
| Referral link | ✅ | ✅ |
| Birthday | ✅ | ✅ |
| Email | — | ✅ |
| Phone | — | ✅ |

Both available on **all plans**. Connect at **Joy Admin → Integrations → [Chatty or Gorgias]**.

## Customer Hub (C:Hub) — blank loyalty panel

The Joy × **Customer Hub (C:Hub)** integration surfaces the loyalty profile inside C:Hub. The loyalty panel can show up **blank** when the dynamic button is clicked. To fix, collect **store access** and escalate to tech to repair the binding (log the case where it stays unresolved).

---

Available on **All plans**. Add a code snippet to theme files to display customer point balance in:
- Navigation menu
- Account page
- Cart page
- Product pages
- Custom page templates

Setup: **Joy Admin → Integrations → Theme integration** for snippet code + placement guide.

---

Available on **Essential, Advanced, Ultimate** (VIP Tier required). Combine Joy VIP tiers with Avada Order Limit's product restrictions for tier-gated catalog access.

## Setup

1. Enable **automatic customer tagging** in Joy (tier name as tag)
2. Configure tier privileges in Joy
3. In Order Limit, restrict products/collections to those tier tags

Note: Joy now has **native exclusive products** via Shopify Functions (kb_vip-tiers) — usually preferable to this older approach.

- kb_vip-tiers (native exclusive products via Shopify Functions)
- kb_settings-developers (theme snippet, magic tags)
- kb_customers (segment-based exclusion)

---

## GoodAPI — redeem points for a real environmental action (tree planting / ocean plastic cleanup)

An alternative redemption type: instead of a discount or coupon, the customer spends points for a real-world environmental action — planting a tree or removing plastic from the ocean. Powered by the third-party Shopify app **GoodAPI (Tree Planting)**. Positioned mainly for higher-tier, on-brand loyalty programs (Plus-tier merchants) rather than a hard plan gate — if a merchant on a lower plan asks, don't assume it's blocked without checking.

**Setup:**
1. Install **GoodAPI (Tree Planting)** from the Shopify App Store and complete its own onboarding.
2. Get a **Sprout API key** from GoodAPI.
3. In Joy: **Integrations → GoodAPI → paste the API key → Connect**. A key prefixed **`TEST-`** is a sandbox key — redemptions using it do not create a real environmental action.
4. Create the redemption program: **Reward programs → Redeeming programs → Add program → Environmental impact** → choose **tree planting** or **ocean plastic cleanup** → set the quantity per redemption and the point cost.
   - After the first redemption on a program, the point cost and quantity can still be edited, but the **impact type** (tree vs plastic) cannot be changed anymore.

**How redemption works:** the customer redeems directly inside the widget — no coupon is generated, no product is created, and the customer never goes through Shopify checkout. GoodAPI confirms the action and the customer's tree/plastic count on their GoodAPI-linked profile increases. If GoodAPI rejects the action, Joy automatically refunds the points to the customer.

**Billing:** GoodAPI charges the merchant directly on the merchant's own GoodAPI account — Joy does not add an extra fee for this feature. The merchant sets their own monthly spend cap on the GoodAPI side before turning a program on.

**Disconnecting:** disconnecting the GoodAPI integration turns off every active environmental-impact redemption program on the shop.

Full guide: `help.joy.so/integrations/goodapi/`.

# Milestone Rewards

Available on **Advanced, Ultimate**. Set up at **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Milestones → Add milestone**.

## Milestone types

| Type | Notes |
|---|---|
| Mixed milestone *(New)* | Sequential journey combining multiple action types |
| Number of orders | Reward on Nth order (e.g. 3rd order) |
| Amount spent | Reward after spending $X total |
| Earned points | Reward after accumulating X points |
| Number of reviews | Reward on Nth review |
| Inactivity | Reward inactive customers to win them back |
| Number of referrals | Reward on Nth successful referral |
| Subscription cycles | Bonus on Nth consecutive billing cycle |

## Reward options (per milestone)

Points, Store credit, Discount amount, Discount percentage, Free gift.

Configure per milestone: name, start/end date, threshold, reward type/value.

## Milestone conditions (per rule)

- **Minimum order requirement** — No minimum / Minimum purchase amount / Minimum quantity of items
- **Anti-cheat** — Set minimum time between orders. Prevents customers from placing multiple orders within a short time frame to game the milestone. Extra orders within the window will not count toward milestones.

## Milestone settings (global)

**Progression mode** — controls what happens when a customer reaches multiple milestones at once:

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Only the highest milestone reward** | Customer gets reward for the highest milestone reached only (e.g. if they hit milestones 1, 2, 3 at once → only reward for #3). Does not apply to Mixed milestones. |
| **All milestone rewards** | Customer gets rewards for every milestone reached (e.g. hit 1, 2, 3 at once → gets all 3 rewards). |

Path: **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Milestones → Milestone settings**

---

Tracks **consecutive successful billing cycles** across a customer's subscription contracts. Use to reduce churn and reward long-term subscribers.

## Required setup

1. Connect **Shopify Flow** at **Joy Admin → Settings → Integrations**
2. Import the Flow template **"Joy Loyalty - Subscription Order Data Sync.flow"** at **Shopify Admin → Apps → Shopify Flow → Import**, then turn it on
   - Required because Shopify doesn't natively send subscription renewal data to apps
3. Create the milestone with:
   - **Milestone condition** — N successful billing cycles
   - **Rewards** — Points, Gift, or Discount

---

Build a journey like: **"Place 3 orders → Write 2 reviews → Refer 1 friend"** — each step must be completed in order before the next unlocks.

Add via **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Milestones → Add milestone → Mixed milestone → Add milestone** for each step.

Step types available: Number of orders, Amount spent, Earned points, Number of reviews, Number of referrals.

---

## Milestone progress on the customer profile

Merchants can see an individual customer's milestone progress without opening Analytics: **Joy Admin → Customers → [customer] → right-hand rail → "Milestone progress" card** (below Referral activities).

- The card lists every active milestone program the customer has progress in: how many steps reached out of the total, a progress bar, and the next threshold + its reward.
- A customer with a reward waiting to be claimed (a Customer's Choice step) shows a **"Reward pending"** chip.
- A customer fully done with a program shows **"All milestones reached"** instead of a next-step line.
- Click **"View milestones"** on the card to open the full ladder for every program the customer has progress in, showing which steps are already reached (✓) vs still locked.
- The card only shows **active, current-generation (V2) milestone programs** the customer has actual progress in — a shop with no active milestone program, or a customer with zero progress anywhere, won't show the card (or shows "No milestone activity yet.").
- **Guest customers never show this card** — milestone progress tracking is member-only.

## Milestone step custom names

Each milestone step (threshold) can optionally get its own **custom name** in the milestone program editor, instead of the default numbered label ("Milestone #1", "Milestone #2", etc.). Once set, the custom name replaces the numbered label everywhere that step is referenced — the admin editor, activity/points log entries, email notifications, and the storefront reward-select popup / milestone ladder. Steps left without a custom name keep showing the default numbered label — fully backward compatible, no action needed on existing programs.

# Analytics

Available on **Essential and above** — the Analytics page is not available on the free Starter plan. Open at **Joy Admin → Analytics**.

## Key metrics

| Metric | What it measures |
|---|---|
| **Revenue by Joy** | Revenue from orders using Joy-issued discounts |
| **Loyalty members** | Total customers who joined the program |
| **Referred revenue** | Sales generated by the referral program |
| **Redemption rate** | % of customers redeeming points (all-time) |
| **Points earned** | Total points earned by all customers |
| **Points redeemed** | Total points redeemed |

Filter by date range to track trends.

## Exporting points activity (Customer name + Order ID + Points earned)

For **point activity over a date range** (not current balances), merchants can self-serve: **Customers → Activities** → set the date range → **Export type = Earned** → enter your email → start export.

Merchants who need a report for accounting/expense reconciliation can export point-earning activity — including **Customer name, Order ID, and Points earned** together in one file. When a merchant asks for this kind of combined export, confirm the exact columns and date range they need; the data is exportable rather than a hard limitation. If the standard in-app export doesn't surface every column they need, collect the store URL + the exact fields + date range and escalate to the team to pull it.

**"Revenue by Joy" / Joy-assisted order data lives in Analytics, not Activities.** Find it at **Joy Dashboard → Analytics → Revenue by Joy** — the order table sits below the chart and can be filtered by date, with an Export button above the chart. Activities is the point-activity audit trail, a different thing.

**A simple "customer + current point balance" list** is a separate export from point-activity: it needs the **Export customers** button enabled first on the Customers page — a one-time backend toggle the team turns on per store on request (not self-serve by default; see kb_customers).

**Join date is not exportable** in either the Activities export or the Export customers list today — don't promise it in a column list.

**Full historical earning/redeeming activity across all customers** (not filtered to a date range) isn't available via the self-serve exports above — it requires a separate backend export from the team; escalate with the store URL and what the data is needed for.

---

Available on **Essential and above**. Joy data is recognized natively in Shopify Analytics — both **loyalty metafields** (Point Balance, VIP Tier) and **Joy tags** (engaged members, assisted orders, referral activity).

## Common reports

- **Revenue by VIP tier** — Gold contribution vs others
- **Retention by tier** — there is **no native repeat-purchase-rate-by-VIP-tier report** today (logged as feedback); use the workaround below
- **Win-back targeting** — high points + no recent order
- **Top spenders by tier** — for VIP-only campaigns
- **AOV by tier** — verify higher tiers spend more

## Requirements

- **Settings → General → Show metafields on Shopify admin** must be ON (kb_settings-general)
- For ShopifyQL: ready-made templates ship in the Joy docs — no need to write queries from scratch

## Repeat-purchase rate by tier (not native yet)

There is **no native report** for repeat-purchase rate broken down by VIP tier — it is logged as product feedback. Workaround: use the **"Returning customers – Joy active redeemers"** metric in **Shopify Analytics**, combined with **auto-tagging active redeemers** (**Settings → Additional features**). Note that **Member-Analytics** figures may be **temporarily unstable** during the current analytics revamp.

## Related
- kb_settings-general (sync metafields requirement)
- kb_settings-order (Joy-assisted order tags)
- kb_settings-misc (auto-tag customers)
- kb_vip-tiers (tier definitions)

---

## Milestone analytics (Rewards tab)

Located at **Joy Admin → Analytics → Rewards tab → Milestones section**. Shows shop-wide milestone performance — separate from the per-customer view on the customer profile (see kb_milestone):

- **KPI cards** — Revenue assisted (orders from customers who hit a milestone), Reward cost (value of milestone rewards granted), Net return.
- **Reward cost by type** — stacked bar breaking cost down by reward type (points, store credit, discount, free gift).
- **Milestone step reach funnel** — all-time, with a program picker to see how many customers reached each step of a specific program.
- **Milestones reached over time** — line chart, respects the page's date filter.
- **Milestone breakdown table** — expandable, per-program detail; also respects the date filter.

Only the funnel widget is all-time; the KPI cards, over-time chart, and breakdown table all follow whatever date range is set on the Analytics page.

# Apple Wallet & Google Wallet Loyalty Pass

Available on **Advanced** plan and above. The pass contains a unique QR/barcode storing customer's loyalty identity — staff scan at POS for instant access to points/tier/rewards.

## Setup at a glance

**Joy Admin → Customers → More actions → Generate digital loyalty pass** → choose **Apple Wallet** or **Google Wallet** → toggle status on → customize design.

To expose the **Add to Wallet** button on storefront: **Theme editor → Customize → Add block → Joy: Loyalty Pass Wallet**.

---

## Pass design

**Customers → Generate pass wallet → Apple Wallet**:
- **Logo** — your brand
- **Colors** — background + text
- **Fields** — customer name, points balance, tier
- **Header** — pass title (e.g., "VIP Member Card")
- **Footer** — extra info / terms

## Push notifications (off by default)

**Notifications tab** of Apple Wallet pass setting. Sends real-time notifications to iPhone lock screen for: points earned, reward applied, tier upgrade, etc. Each type must be manually enabled.

### Notifications from other connected apps (cross-app wallet alerts)

Other Avada apps can push their own notifications onto a customer's existing Joy wallet pass — the pass still carries the Joy brand, but the alert content comes from the other app. Confirmed working with **Wishlist Plus** (price-drop / back-in-stock alerts) and **Joy Subscription** (renewal reminders); other apps that call the same wallet-notification hook (via a Shopify Flow action or API) should also qualify.

**Enable at:** Customers → Generate digital loyalty pass → Apple Wallet (or Google Wallet) → **Notifications tab** → turn on **"Notifications from connected apps."** This is a separate toggle from Joy's own notification types (points earned, tier upgrade, etc.) above, and is off by default.

**Requirements:**
- The customer must have already added the Joy Wallet Pass to their phone.
- The other app must actively trigger the notification via a **Shopify Flow action** (send wallet notification) or via **API** — it does not fire automatically just because both apps are installed.

The alert shows on the customer's phone lock screen exactly like Joy's own wallet notifications; tapping it opens the Joy pass.

## Requirements

- Joy plan: Advanced+
- Apple Wallet pass enabled and saved in Joy admin
- Customer must have added pass to their Apple Wallet

---

**Customers → More actions → Generate digital loyalty pass → Google Wallet** → toggle status On → customize.

## Notification triggers

- Earning points
- Receiving a discount/reward
- Tier upgrade or status change
- Points expiring soon
- Coupon expiring soon (merchant picks days-ahead, e.g. 3 days)
- Coupon expired (fires the moment it becomes invalid)

A notification only sends when **all** conditions are met: Google Wallet enabled for the shop + that notification type is on + the relevant event fires.

---

## Steps for staff at POS

1. Open Shopify POS → **Customers** → Add customer (name, email, phone, DOB) or search existing
2. Open Joy → look up the customer → **Generate digital loyalty pass**
3. Have customer scan the on-screen QR with their phone camera
4. **Apple Wallet** (iOS): customer taps Add to Apple Wallet
5. **Google Wallet** (Android with Google Wallet app): customer taps Add to Google Wallet

# Redeeming Programs

Set up at **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Redeeming programs**.

> Plan names below use current naming: **Starter** (free), **Essential**, **Advanced**, **Ultimate**. "Pro" is the legacy name for **Essential** — if any older material says "Pro", read it as Essential.

| Program | Plans |
|---|---|
| Discount (amount, %, BXGY) | All |
| Free gift | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |
| Free shipping | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |
| Gift Card | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |
| Coupon list at checkout | Ultimate (Shopify Plus + Checkout Extensibility) |
| Redeem at checkout page | Ultimate (Shopify Plus + Checkout Extensibility); Advanced via sales contact |
| Total/per-customer redemption limits | All |

When customers redeem, Joy generates a unique one-time-use coupon code.

## How customers actually redeem

The main path is the widget or loyalty page: the customer logs in, opens the widget, goes to **Redeem points**, picks a reward and clicks **Redeem**. They then either click **Apply** to push the code to the cart, or copy the code and paste it at checkout.

**The code does not apply itself at checkout.** This is the single most common "my discount vanished" report — points were spent, the code was issued and is valid, but nobody entered it. Unused codes are always retrievable from the widget's **My coupons** section.

Other redemption surfaces: the **cart drawer** (kb_cart-drawer), **checkout page** (Quick Redeem / coupon list / redeem-at-checkout, see below), and **POS** (staff look up the balance and apply the reward to the cart).

One quirk: if a customer clicks Apply while their cart is empty, the discount is held and takes effect once items are added — the page may need a refresh before the cart reflects it.

**Minimum order value is checked at the moment the coupon is applied at checkout, not at redemption.** So a customer can redeem anytime, but the discount only takes effect once their cart reaches the minimum. Joy displays the minimum automatically wherever the reward appears — e.g. "Applicable for $85 minimum orders" — on the widget, loyalty page, and again in the coupon details under My Rewards after redemption; the condition is never hidden. For Free Gift rewards, merchants can also add their own description to a reward, shown on the widget and loyalty page.

**A redeemed reward is an order-level discount, applied once per order regardless of item quantity.** A merchant with 2+ units of a product in the cart will see the same discount amount as with 1 unit — there is no per-unit multiplication or per-unit cap on a redeemed reward's value. This is expected behaviour, not a bug.

---

## Discount types

- **Discount amount** — fixed $ off
- **Discount percentage** — % off
- **Buy X Get Y (BXGY)** — buy quantity → get extra products/discounts

## Redeem value modes

- **Dynamic Discount** — flexible point thresholds. Optional limits:
  - Minimum points required to redeem
  - Maximum points per redemption
  - Maximum discount % of cart total
- **Fixed Discount** — set $ amount per redemption

## Settings

- **Applicable categories** — products/collections discount applies to
- **Minimum order requirement** — cart minimum
- **Coupon expiration date** — when an individual generated code expires (separate from the reward's own Start/End date, see below)
- **Combinations** — which Shopify discount classes can stack
- **Sales channels** — where the discount is valid

## Redemption program Start/End date

Every redemption program (discount, free gift, free shipping, gift card, etc.) has a **Start/End date** setting, with a **"No end date"** toggle that is **on by default** — existing reward programs keep working unchanged unless a merchant explicitly sets an end date.

- **Start date** — the reward isn't offered for redemption before this date.
- **End date** — once it passes, the reward **automatically hides from new redemption** (customers can no longer redeem it). This is separate from a code's own **Coupon expiration date**: codes customers **already claimed before the end date remain valid** and usable until their own individual expiry — an expired program end date does not retroactively invalidate codes already in customers' hands.
- This is an extension of the older "coupon expiration date" concept: coupon expiration controls when an issued code expires, while Start/End date controls when the reward itself is available to be redeemed at all.

## Reward visibility when restricted to a Shopify customer segment

When a redemption program's **"Who can use this reward"** is set to a specific **Shopify customer segment**, the reward is now **fully hidden from ineligible customers** — it does not appear on the widget, loyalty page, or storefront for anyone outside the segment.

**This is a behavior change.** Previously, a segment-restricted reward was still visible to everyone but blocked/unusable for customers outside the segment. If a merchant or a confused customer asks why a reward "disappeared" even though it used to show up, this is expected: the reward is working as intended, just now hidden instead of shown-but-blocked for non-eligible customers.

---

Available on Essential, Advanced, Ultimate.

## Selection modes

- **Free one product from selection** (default) — customer picks one
- **Free all products in selection** — useful for bundles

**Only products published to the Online Store sales channel sync to Joy and appear in the reward product picker.** Products left as Draft, or removed from the Online Store channel, won't be selectable. If a merchant wants a reward product that shouldn't be publicly browsable: keep the product **Active** in Shopify (it must stay Active for the program to reference it) but hide the Buy button — group reward products under a dedicated product template and hide the Buy button on that template — or combine with a VIP tier perk (**Membership → VIP Tiers → [tier] → Tier privileges → Exclusive products/collections**) to restrict purchase while still allowing point redemption.

### Changing the selected product after redeeming a Free Gift

Once a customer redeems a Free Gift reward and picks a product, **the code is locked to that product** — there's no direct "change my pick" action. The only way to swap it is if **Enable Customer Self-Revoke Coupon** is turned on (**Settings → Additional Features**): the customer revokes the unused coupon themselves, the points return to their balance, and they can re-redeem and pick a different product.

**Not available on the Account Page (Loyalty Hub)** — self-revoke and redeem-from-cart only work from the **widget or loyalty page**, due to Shopify Customer Account platform limitations. If a merchant only offers the Account Page experience, a customer wanting to change their free-gift pick needs the widget/loyalty page instead, or a manual revoke by the merchant.

Also note: a Free Gift reward can't be injected directly at the Shopify **checkout** page (a Shopify platform limit) — it must be applied via **Apply** in the widget/loyalty page first, same as other redemption types.

### "Too many products/variants" error on a discount program
If a merchant hits a discount-selection limit error even though they picked fewer than 100 **products**, the limit actually counts **variants**, not products — a handful of multi-variant products can add up to 100+ variants quickly. This is a hard cap from **Shopify's own Discount API**, not a Joy setting, and Joy can't raise it. Workaround: group the products into a Shopify **Collection** and select the collection instead of individual products/variants.

### Free Product / perk reward shows "unavailable" or "out of stock" even though the product is actually in stock
**Cause:** a reward or VIP perk references a product by its Shopify **variant ID**. If the merchant later edits that product's variants in Shopify (e.g. adds/removes an option, re-creates variants), Shopify assigns **new internal variant IDs** — the reward program still points at the old, now-stale ID, so Joy can't resolve it and shows the product as unavailable/out of stock even though the current product is in stock.
**Fix:** remove the product from the reward/perk and re-add the **current** version of the product — this re-links the program to the live variant ID. This does not affect actual redemption eligibility once re-linked; if it's still wrong after re-adding, escalate with the product URL and a screenshot.

### Reward pointing to a deleted or archived product

**Old behavior (before this fix):** if a merchant deleted or archived a product used as a Free Gift or a discount-eligible product, the reward stayed redeemable — the customer's points were deducted, and only at **Add to cart** did they see "SOLD OUT." The merchant had no way to know the program was broken until a customer complained.

**Current behavior:** Joy now checks the products a reward references. If **every** product a reward points to is deleted/archived/unavailable, the **Redeem button is disabled** with an explanatory message, and the customer is **not charged points**. If only some products in a multi-product selection are unavailable, the reward stays redeemable for the remaining valid ones.

- A **banner on the Joy Home page** lists every broken reward program with a direct link to fix it — resolving the product reference and reloading the page clears the banner.
- Merchants who don't check the admin regularly still get a **summary email** listing the affected programs.

If a merchant asks why a reward suddenly can't be redeemed, check whether the underlying product was deleted or archived in Shopify — this warning system is the likely cause, not a bug.

## Variants

- For multi-variant products, you can mark specific variants or all as eligible
- If multiple eligible variants are in cart, discount applies to the **lowest-priced variant** automatically

## Settings

Discount combinations, sales channels, usage restrictions (everyone vs only redeemer), coupon expiration, refund-on-cancel, custom code prefix.

Customers select the product in the loyalty widget when redeeming.

Essential, Advanced, Ultimate. Same setup as discount: points cost, minimum order, combinations (stack with order/product discounts), sales channels, expiration, refund-on-cancel.

Unused coupons can be revoked and converted back to points by merchant on customer request — **Joy Admin → Customers → [name] → Revoke coupon**.

**Once a coupon has been generated, its conditions and expiry cannot be edited.** If a customer's coupon is about to expire or has expired, the practical fix is to issue a replacement discount code — either revoke and let them re-redeem, or create a code directly in Shopify Admin → Discounts. Expired coupons are automatically hidden from the widget, so customers won't see dead codes.

**Note: changing Combinations only affects newly issued coupons** — codes already in customers' hands keep the settings they were created with.

### Deactivate a coupon WITHOUT refunding points

**Revoke** always converts the unused coupon **back into points** — that is by design, and there is no toggle to "revoke without refund" and no bulk-deactivate in Joy.

- To **disable a code but keep the points spent**, deactivate the code **directly in Shopify → Discounts** (do **not** use Joy's Revoke). Note: after deactivating in Shopify, the coupon's status inside Joy may not auto-update to Expired — if the merchant needs the app status synced, escalate.
- To **deactivate many/all coupons at once without refunding** (e.g. before re-launching a new redeem program), there is no self-serve UI — escalate with the store URL and the list/criteria of coupons to disable. Append `<escalate_human>`.

## Gift Card redeem program

Available on Essential, Advanced, Ultimate.

A **Gift Card** redeem program lets customers exchange points for a **real, reusable Shopify gift card** — not a one-time-use coupon like the other redeem types. The card has its own **balance** and can be spent down gradually across **multiple orders**, just like any gift card issued directly in Shopify.

- **Setup:** **Reward programs → create redeem program → choose type "Gift Card"**. The first time a merchant sets this up, Joy requires granting the app **gift-card permission** in Shopify before the program can be created.
- **On redeem:** the customer can choose to keep the gift card for themselves, or enter a friend's email to send it directly to that person — Shopify sends the gift card to the recipient.
- **Code visibility (security):** the **full gift card code is shown only once**, at the moment of issuance. After that, only the **last 4 digits** are visible — including to the store owner in Shopify Admin. This matches Shopify's own standard gift-card behavior and is not a Joy-specific limitation.

## Send Gift to a Friend (Free Gift rewards)

After a customer redeems a **Free Gift** reward, they get a **"Send to a friend"** option that lets them send the gift coupon directly to someone else — entering the friend's email, name, and a message — instead of, or in addition to, keeping it for themselves.

- **Enable at:** Free Gift program → turn on "Send to Friend" and choose a delivery/automation method.
- **Delivery methods (3):** Joy's built-in email, **Shopify Flow**, or **Klaviyo** — same automation options as Referral. For Joy's built-in email, the template is under **Settings → Notifications → "Send gift to friend"**.
- **Where it appears:** the main widget, loyalty page, My Rewards, and Customer Account.
- **Rate limit (Joy in-app sending only):** fixed at **100 emails/day** total and **1 recipient per 24 hours**, to prevent spam/abuse. This limit is **not merchant-configurable**.

---

Both require **Shopify Plus + Checkout Extensibility** and **Ultimate** plan (Advanced via sales contact).

## Coupon list at checkout

Shows previously redeemed unused coupons inline at checkout. Customer applies in one click. Add via **Reward programs → Redeem programs → [program] → Set up here → Add app block → Joy Coupon List**.

## Redeem at checkout page

Lets customer convert points to discount **directly at checkout**, no widget needed. Toggle on in the program's Redeem value section. Cancel = points refunded instantly.

**Limitation:** Checkout UI extensions don't support i18n by IP/browser. Theme Editor lets you set one main language only.

---

In each program's **Redemption limit** card:
- **Program total limitation** — overall cap (e.g. 50)
- **Each customer's limit** — per-customer cap (optional)

Whichever cap hits first stops further redemptions. When total limit is reached, reward shows **Sold out** in widget. Reset manually via the Reset button next to the counter (cannot be undone). Limits can be edited live without affecting existing redemptions. Only completed redeems count.

## Per-customer limit uses a rolling window (known limitation)
The per-customer / daily redemption limit counts time as a **rolling 24-hour cycle**, not a reset at the store timezone's midnight. So a customer who redeems at 5pm stays locked until 5pm the next day, not until midnight. This can feel unexpected (e.g. locked out at 10am the morning after an evening purchase). There is currently **no merchant-facing setting to switch to a midnight reset** — this is logged product feedback under review by the team. Don't promise a fix date; acknowledge it as a known limitation.

# Points — Advanced Settings & Store Credit

Store credit grants real cash-value balance on the customer's Shopify account, applied **automatically at checkout** — no coupons. Powered by Shopify's native store credit.

## Plan availability

- All plans — earning programs (Place Order, etc.)
- Advanced & Ultimate — Milestones, Referrals, Shopify Flow

## Points vs Store Credit

| | Points | Store Credit |
|---|---|---|
| Customer experience | Redeem for coupon | Auto-applied at checkout |
| Perceived value | Abstract ("500 pts") | Concrete ("$5.00") |
| Friction | Manual redemption | None |
| Best for | Gamified, tiered programs | Simple cashback |

## Enabling

When you select **Store Credit** as reward type in any supported program for the first time, an inline banner prompts **Grant Access**. Click → **Confirm** to authorize Joy to manage Shopify store credit balances. One-time grant covers all programs.

## Store credit shown across the storefront

Store credit is no longer only visible at checkout. Joy now surfaces the customer's **store credit balance + how much they'll earn** across the storefront, so the reward stays visible and pulls customers back:

- **Where it shows:** widget **Balance card**, loyalty page, account pages, **Point calculator**, thank you page, and the reward listing of any program whose reward type is Store Credit.
- **No toggle needed** — it appears automatically when **both** are true: the shop has **granted Store Credit permission** AND has **at least one active Store Credit program**.
- Balance is shown in the **shop's currency**.
- **In the Unified widget**, customize it on the **Balance card**: choose the design style, show or hide the store credit value, etc.

## Store credit mechanics

- **Calculated on the order subtotal** — shipping and tax are excluded. To also exclude gift cards from the earning base, add an **Advanced condition** on the rule.
- **Rate is simplified by default** — Joy reduces the displayed rate to its simplest form (e.g. an earn rate that works out to $2 store credit per $100 spent displays as $1 store credit per $50 spent). Store credit amounts always render as a currency value ("$X store credit"), never as a bare countable "credit(s)" — if a merchant reports seeing old-style "N credits" wording anywhere, that surface is stale and should be flagged to the team. The **"don't simplify"** checkbox changes the **display only**, not the actual earning rate.
- **Rounding** — with the **Nearest** rounding option, a small order can round down to **$0**. To issue exact fractional amounts, enable **decimal store credit**.
- **Per-VIP-tier store-credit rates** are supported (set a different rate on each tier).
- **"Failed to adjust store credit"** error — re-grant access (re-run the Grant Access / Confirm step above).

---

Set up at **Reward programs → Point Expiration → Turn on**.

| Type | Plans | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Full point expiration | Essential+ | Whole balance expires after N days of inactivity. Any earn/spend resets the timer for the entire balance |
| Fixed date expiration | Essential+ | All points expire on a specific calendar date regardless of when earned |
| Expiration by earning date (FIFO) | Ultimate only | Each batch of points expires N days after it was earned |

Example for Full expiration set to 365: customer earns Jan 1 → expires Dec 31 unless they engage; new purchase June 1 extends all to next May 31.

### Troubleshooting: points expired sooner than expected
- Confirm which expiration type is on (Full inactivity / Fixed date / FIFO).
- For **Full expiration**, the clock runs on the **last activity (earn OR spend)**, not the last order date, and it resets for the **whole** balance on any activity. A common cause of "expired too early" is that the setting was **turned on or changed earlier** and the merchant forgot, or the inactivity clock is measured from an **older earn**, not the most recent order.
- Check the customer's activity log for the `expired` event date and compare it to the last activity. If the expiry date doesn't match any of the three logics above, escalate so the team can check the setting's history — append `<escalate_human>`.

### Adjusting a customer's points has a floor of 0
- You **cannot** push a balance **negative** — the minimum adjustment is **0**. If a merchant over-credited and needs to remove more than the customer currently has, they can only remove down to the current balance.
- Adjusting a balance to **0** clears the available points for **that customer only** — it is not a shop-wide reset. Resetting points for **all** customers requires a CSV import / team tooling.
- Adjusting the point balance does **not** re-sync **VIP tier points** (separate metric) — see kb_vip-tiers.

### Manual point adjustments and VIP tier calculation
- By default, points added or removed manually at **Customers → [customer] → adjust points** do **not** count toward VIP tier progress — only points from configured earning programs feed the tier calculation. This is why a customer given a manual bonus can show little or no movement toward their next tier.
- To make a specific manual adjustment count toward tier progress too, check the **"include in tier calculation"** option shown on the adjustment dialog when adding or subtracting points.

---

## Refund points (All plans)

Off by default per program. Enable at **Reward programs → Redeem programs → [program] → Turn on Refund Points**. When merchant cancels the order:
- Customer's money is refunded
- Points used in the redemption are refunded (the coupon itself is not)
- Partial refunds calculate proportional points per item
- Only **fully cancelled** orders refund points used; **partial cancellations don't refund points** for the removed items

Place-order earning rules also have an auto-revoke toggle for cancelled/refunded orders.

## Pending points (Advanced, Ultimate)

Holds earned points in a pending state for a configured waiting period before converting to Available Points. Use to align with your return window and reduce fraud.

Enable at **Joy Admin → Settings → Additional Features → Pending Points → Turn on**, then set the waiting period (e.g., 8 days). Pending points don't redeem and don't count toward tier status until they convert.

## Limiting how many points a customer can earn

A hard cap on a customer's **total point balance** is not supported. To cap **how much they can earn**, use:
- **Limit customer earning** (Advanced) at **Settings → Additional features** — caps the maximum points a customer can earn within a chosen **timeframe**.
- **Maximum points per order** on the **Place order** program — caps the points awarded on any single order.

---

## Discount combinations (Essential+)

Each discount belongs to one of Shopify's three discount classes: **Product**, **Order**, or **Shipping**. In the redeeming program's **Combinations** setting, pick which classes the Joy coupon is allowed to combine with. Reference: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/discounts/discount-combinations

### Shopify's combination rules (apply to every store, not just Joy)
- **Product + Shipping** — always combinable, no restriction.
- **Order + Shipping** — always combinable, no restriction.
- **Product + Product** — combinable, but only on **different line items**. Two product discounts cannot both apply to the **same item** unless the store is on **Shopify Plus** with tag-based configuration for same-item stacking.
- **Product + Order** and **Order + Order** — combinable only for **eligible merchants**: the store must have **no checkout.liquid customizations** and must **not use the Licensify app**. If the merchant isn't eligible, these classes can't combine no matter what Joy's Combinations setting says.
- **Shipping + Shipping** — cannot combine with another shipping discount, ever.

### Other limits merchants may hit
- **Automatic discounts:** max **25 active per store** (this includes app-generated ones like Joy's).
- **Discount codes per order:** up to **5 product/order codes** + **1 shipping code**.
- **Application order:** Product discounts apply first, then Order discounts (calculated on the subtotal *after* the product discount), then Shipping discounts.
- **Stacking percentages:** when multiple Order discounts are % based, each is calculated on the **original subtotal** — they don't compound on top of each other.
- **Sales channel:** combinable discounts only combine on orders through **Online Store, Storefront API, or Shopify POS** — other channels may not honor the combination.
- If a customer enters a non-combinable code: Shopify shows "Discount couldn't be used with your existing discounts", or (when multiple non-combinable discounts would otherwise conflict) **auto-applies whichever discount is best for the customer's cart**.
- Changing a program's combination settings affects only **newly redeemed** coupons, not codes already issued.

### Troubleshooting checklist when a Joy code won't combine
1. Identify the Joy coupon's discount class (Product/Order/Shipping) and the other active discount's class.
2. Check Shopify's base rule above for that class pair — some pairs (Product+Product same item, Order+Order, Product+Order) only combine for eligible merchants or Shopify Plus.
3. If the class pair is eligible, confirm the Joy redeeming program's **Combinations** setting actually has that class turned on.
4. If everything above checks out and it still fails, escalate — append `<escalate_human>`.

## Sales channels

In Place Order: choose **Online store only**, **Online store & POS**, **POS only**, or **Online store and Admin draft orders** (POS channel needs Pro + POS plan and above). By default, Place Order programs only reward orders placed through the storefront — an order created as a **draft order in Shopify Admin** (e.g. by staff, or via a POS-adjacent workflow) does **not** earn points unless the program's Sales channel setting is switched to include **"Online store and Admin draft orders."** If a merchant reports a specific order didn't earn points and that order turns out to be an admin-created draft order, this setting — not a bug — is almost always the cause. Redeeming programs let you scope coupons to specific channels — applies to newly created codes only.

---

Available on **Advanced, Ultimate**. Every earning rule you create runs independently. On any qualifying action, Joy evaluates all active programs and applies every one whose conditions are met — they **stack**.

## Common patterns

- **Always-on base rule**: 1 pt/$1 on all orders
- **Collection bonus**: 2× points on "Summer Collection"
- **Seasonal campaigns**: bonus during Black Friday week
- **Customer-segment targeting**: bonus for VIP tier or specific tags
- **Time-of-week boosters**: weekend or after-hours bonuses
- **Birthday-month booster**: extra multiplier in customer's birth month

Rules don't replace each other unless conditions prevent overlap.

## Sandbox mode (All plans)

**Reward programs → Sandbox Mode → Turn on** lets you test setup without awarding points to real customers. Add designated test accounts; only those earn during testing. Banner appears in admin while sandbox is active.
